A grammar chapter that pulls together the present tense you've been meeting verb by verb. Three things to take away: the **بـ prefix**, the **four personal prefixes**, and the fact that verbs come in **types** that share one set of endings. Tap any example to reveal its franco and English.

## The بـ prefix

A bare present verb in Egyptian carries a **بـ (bi‑)** in front. That prefix is what marks an everyday present — a habit or something going on right now:

- **بكتب (baktib)** = "I write / I'm writing"
- **بيشتغل (biyishta8al)** = "he works / he's working"

Drop the بـ and you get the **bare form** used after words like عايز (want), لازم (must) and ممكن (can) — *3ayez aroo7* "I want to go". That bare form has its own grammar chapter; here everything keeps its بـ.

## The four personal prefixes

Whatever the verb, the present is built from the same small set of prefixes — **ba‑ / bit‑ / biy‑ / bin‑** — plus an **‑i** ending for إنتِ and an **‑u** ending for the plurals. Here is the skeleton on a regular verb, **كتب (katab)** "to write":

| Pronoun     | Present             | Built from |
|-------------|---------------------|------------|
| أنا - ana   | بكتب - baktib       | ba‑        |
| إنت - inta  | بتكتب - bitiktib    | bit‑       |
| إنتِ - inti  | بتكتبي - bitiktibi  | bit‑ … ‑i  |
| هو - huwwa  | بيكتب - biyiktib    | biy‑       |
| هي - hiyya  | بتكتب - bitiktib    | bit‑       |
| إحنا - e7na | بنكتب - biniktib    | bin‑       |
| إنتو - intu | بتكتبوا - bitiktibu | bit‑ … ‑u  |
| هم - humma  | بيكتبوا - biyiktibu | biy‑ … ‑u  |

Learn those four prefixes once and they never change. What *does* change is the middle of the verb — and that depends on its **type**.

## Verb types

Egyptian verbs fall into a few families by the shape of their root. The prefixes above stay the same; the stem behaves differently. Here is one of each, with the chapter where you met it.

| Type | Verb | أنا (ana) | هو (huwwa) | Seen in |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| Regular (solid root) | فهم - fehem (understand) | بفهم - bafham | بيفهم - biyifham | Speaking & Understanding |
| Regular (solid root) | كتب - katab (write) | بكتب - baktib | بيكتب - biyiktib | Everyday Verbs |
| Hollow (weak middle) | راح - raa7 (go) | بروح - baroo7 | بيروح - biyroo7 | Verbs of Movement |
| Hollow (weak middle) | نام - naam (sleep) | بنام - banam | بينام - biynam | Daily Routine |
| Final-weak | صحى - se7i (wake up) | بصحى - bas7a | بيصحى - biys7a | Daily Routine |
| Doubled | حب - 7abb (love) | بحب - ba7ebb | بيحب - biy7ebb | Liking, Wanting, Disliking |
| اتـ‑verb | اتكلم - itkallim (speak) | بتكلم - batkallim | بيتكلم - biyitkallim | Speaking & Understanding |

The pattern to notice: a **hollow** verb shows a long vowel in the middle (roo7, naam), a **final-weak** verb ends in ‑a or ‑i, a **doubled** verb doubles its last consonant (7abb), and an **اتـ‑verb** simply keeps its اتـ. None of that touches the four prefixes.

## The participle

Not everything "happening now" is a بـ verb. For **states** — wanting, knowing,
going, living — Egyptian often uses a **participle**: an adjective-like word
that agrees in gender and number and takes **no بـ**.

| English       | m.   | franco | f.    | franco | pl.    | franco  |
|---------------|------|--------|-------|--------|--------|---------|
| wanting       | عايز | 3ayez  | عايزة | 3ayza  | عايزين | 3ayzin  |
| knowing       | عارف | 3aref  | عارفة | 3arfa  | عارفين | 3arfin  |
| going         | رايح | raye7  | رايحة | ray7a  | رايحين | ray7in  |
| understanding | فاهم | fahem  | فاهمة | fahma  | فاهمين | fahmin  |
| living        | عايش | 3ayish | عايشة | 3aysha | عايشين | 3ayshin |

Because a participle isn't a verb, you negate it with **مش (mesh)**, not with ما...ش: *mesh 3ayez* "I don't want", *mesh fahem* "I don't understand".

## Examples

<details class="frase">

<summary>بكتب كل يوم</summary>

[baktib kol yom]{.fr} [I write every day (habit)]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>بيشتغل دلوقتي</summary>

[biyishta8al delwa2ti]{.fr} [he's working now (ongoing)]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>أنا عايز قهوة</summary>

[ana 3ayez 2ahwa]{.fr} [I want a coffee (participle, no بـ)]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>هي رايحة الشغل</summary>

[hiyya rayha el-sho8l]{.fr} [she's going to work (participle, f.)]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>مش فاهم</summary>

[mesh fahem]{.fr} [I don't understand]{.en}

</details>

## Exercises

Try each one out loud first, then tap **Show answer**.

### Exercise 1 — Build the present

Add the right prefix and ending.

**1.** هو + كتب

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[بيكتب]{.ar} [huwwa biyiktib]{.fr}

</details>

**2.** إحنا + فهم

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[بنفهم]{.ar} [e7na binfham]{.fr}

</details>

**3.** إنتِ + راح

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[بتروحي]{.ar} [inti bitroo7i]{.fr}

</details>

**4.** هم + نام

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[بيناموا]{.ar} [humma biynamu]{.fr}

</details>

### Exercise 2 — Translate into Arabic

**1.** I write every day.

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[بكتب كل يوم]{.ar} [baktib kol yom]{.fr}

</details>

**2.** He's working now.

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[بيشتغل دلوقتي]{.ar} [biyishta8al delwa2ti]{.fr}

</details>

**3.** I want a coffee.

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[أنا عايز قهوة]{.ar} [ana 3ayez 2ahwa]{.fr}

</details>

### Exercise 3 — Verb or participle?

Give the form and remember: participles negate with مش.

**1.** I don't understand. *(participle)*

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[مش فاهم]{.ar} [mesh fahem]{.fr}

</details>

**2.** she wants *(participle, f.)*

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[عايزة]{.ar} [3ayza]{.fr}

</details>

**3.** I know *(participle, m.)*

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[عارف]{.ar} [3aref]{.fr}

</details>
